content: Acid Red 2 is an indicator dye that exhibits a red coloration in acidic solutions. It belongs to the azo dye class and appears as a dark red crystalline powder. In microbiology, methyl red is utilized in the Methyl Red (MR) Test, which is designed to identify bacteria capable of producing stable acids through the mixed acid fermentation of glucose. This test is often compared to the Voges-Proskauer (VP) test. Murexide and methyl red have been studied as potential enhancers for the sonochemical degradation of chlorinated hydrocarbon pollutants. Methyl red is classified by the International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) as a Group 3 substance, meaning it is not classifiable regarding its carcinogenicity to humans. The associated risk phrases for methyl red include R20 (harmful by inhalation), R21 (harmful in contact with skin), R22 (harmful if swallowed), R36 (irritating to eyes), R37 (irritating to respiratory system), R38 (irritating to skin), and R40 (limited evidence of a carcinogenic effect).
